minutes.headline: Board leans toward a special meeting to fund a pilot study on adding Keating wells to PFAS treatment
minutes.summary: The Water District Commissioners reviewed the ongoing Rolling Acres water main project, discussed doing future main replacement in-house versus hiring it out and a possible multi-year warrant article for equipment and staff, and heard a clerk's report on PFAS settlement checks and legal limits on spending them. A lengthy public comment period featured a resident pressing the board to add a combined Keating-well/Lancaster treatment option to its public survey, which the board said would require a DEP-mandated pilot study and likely its own warrant article at a special meeting; no formal vote was taken on that question.

what_happened.line: Board leaned toward calling a special meeting to fund a DEP-required pilot study on adding a combined Keating-well/Lancaster treatment option, but took no vote.
Counsel told the board it cannot spend PFAS settlement funds without specific votes, contrary to what commissioners had assumed.
The board discussed appropriating settlement money for test wells before the annual meeting, since funds voted there aren't available until July.
Commissioners compared in-house versus contracted water main replacement and floated a multi-year warrant article for equipment and crew, without resolving it.
The public survey on future treatment options will stay open roughly 30 to 60 days while the district plans outreach.

why_it_matters: A pilot study and any related equipment purchase would likely require a warrant article at a special town meeting, a vote residents would be asked to take.
How PFAS settlement money can be spent is now constrained by a legal-vote requirement the board says it did not previously understand, affecting the pace of well and treatment work.
The treatment-option survey open to residents may or may not include a combined Keating-well option, pending confirmation of DEP pilot-study requirements.
